name: Carya

project_scope.selection_mode: Genus comparison lesson from live Master Plant Pool and existing Juglandaceae family module
project_scope.admission_note: Both taxa are present in the approved Master Plant Pool. This lesson does not install, promote, or change range status for either species.

shared_genus_characters.look_here_first: Start with the alternate pinnately compound leaf, then confirm a husked nut. For species ID, move quickly to the mature husk + nut rather than relying on leaflet count.
shared_genus_characters.vegetative: Woody Juglandaceae with alternate odd-pinnately compound leaves and aromatic/resinous foliage; male flowers occur in catkins.
shared_genus_characters.reproductive: Unisexual flowers; mature fruit is a nut enclosed by a husk that splits along sutures.
shared_genus_characters.genus_confirmation: Compound leaf + catkins + a sutured husk around a hard nut places the plant in the local hickory/pecan doorway rather than an oak or walnut look-alike.

species_comparison_matrix.look_first: Mature nut shape and husk thickness
species_comparison_matrix.fruit: Nut characteristically compressed and 2-angled, with a rough/warty surface; husk comparatively thin.
species_comparison_matrix.leaf: Usually fewer leaflets than pecan, but counts overlap and should remain supporting evidence only.
species_comparison_matrix.best_separator: A mature compressed, angled, rough nut inside a thin husk is the strongest project teaching character.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Do not identify water hickory from leaflet number alone.

species_comparison_matrix.look_first: Mature nut shape and husk thickness
species_comparison_matrix.fruit: Nut uncompressed and not 2-angled, comparatively smooth and elongate; husk distinctly thicker than in water hickory.
species_comparison_matrix.leaf: Often carries more leaflets than water hickory, but the ranges overlap.
species_comparison_matrix.best_separator: Use the elongate smooth uncompressed nut plus the thick husk; leaflet number is secondary.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Ornamental/managed pecans may be encountered outside obviously natural settings, so habitat is not a diagnostic character.

decision_sequence: Confirm Juglandaceae/Carya architecture: alternate pinnately compound leaves + catkins + husked nut.
Photograph or collect a naturally fallen mature fruit when available; do not force the species ID from foliage alone.
Compressed, 2-angled, rough/warty nut + thin husk → C. aquatica door.
Uncompressed, unangled, smoother elongate nut + thick husk → C. illinoinensis door.
Use leaflet count only as supporting evidence.
If fruit characters are intermediate, do not force the ID; C. aquatica and C. illinoinensis are documented to hybridize.
overlap_and_cautions: Leaflet counts overlap and are not the primary separator.
Both species can occur in wet bottomland/riparian settings, so habitat alone is unsafe.
Carya aquatica and C. illinoinensis can hybridize; intermediate fruit characters deserve a Genus Diagnostic Review handoff rather than a forced species label.
Flower color and general tree silhouette are low-value characters for this comparison.

realistic_lookalikes.separate_by: Stay with fruit architecture: Carya husks split along sutures around a hickory/pecan nut; use the existing Juglandaceae family lesson for walnut twig/pith and fruit context.
Require reproductive confirmation with catkins and the husked nut rather than identifying from compound leaves alone.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.purpose: Teach the strongest species separator directly.
Make husk thickness and nut geometry visible in one frame.
Teach leaflet-count tendency while explicitly showing why it is secondary.
Genus/family confirmation rather than species separation.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.target: suspected C. aquatica × C. illinoinensis material if project media becomes available

media_routing.existing_project_media: Reuse any exact Carya fruit/nut or leaf media already present in project/user material when it clearly shows the diagnostic role.
media_routing.instruction: Highest-value acquisition is a same-scale mature fruit/nut comparison. Do not prioritize generic whole-tree glamour images over fruit geometry.

diagnostic_review_handoffs: If a specimen has intermediate C. aquatica/C. illinoinensis fruit characters, route the exact observation to Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review because hybridization is documented.
Species taxonomy/range certification and canonical installation remain outside this genus lesson lane.
